regulator: Individual state (and D.C./territory) physical therapy licensing boards license practice; the Federation of State Boards of Physical Therapy (FSBPT) administers the national exam (NPTE) and coordinates credentialing standards; the Foreign Credentialing Commission on Physical Therapy (FCCPT) is a recognized credential-evaluation and visa-screening agency.
oet_note: OET is NOT universally accepted. The authoritative FSBPT Jurisdiction Licensure Reference Guide lists ONLY the TOEFL iBT as the English test referenced across state boards, and FSBPT/USCIS guidance states TOEFL is the exam accepted for PTs; many individual state boards require TOEFL specifically (or require no test). However, the credential evaluator FCCPT — which performs English-language verification for its Type 1 licensure evaluations (used by CA, LA, MA, NE, NM, ND, TN, D.C.) and for USCIS visa screening — DOES accept the OET among several tests (with minimums roughly Reading 340 / Listening 320 / Writing 350 / Speaking 360), alongside TOEFL iBT, IELTS Academic, Pearson PTE, Cambridge and the Michigan English Test. Net effect: OET may satisfy FCCPT's English verification and thus some pathways, but TOEFL is the dominant/safe choice and the only test many state boards name. Applicants must confirm with their specific state board, since state rules control.
